ordered_controls.meaning: A prior active receipt must not acknowledge the next policy request after an actual descriptor creation.
A prior active receipt must not authorize a repeated write after an actual completed write.
A prior active receipt must not authorize a repeated audit or another old action.
A prior active receipt must not authorize a second close after the one confirmed close attempt.
Every continued active reply is bound to this request by sequence + 1.
A different future sequence is not the response to this request.
Terminal output keeps the current request sequence; it does not use a new or earlier value.
Initial output is the unique active MEMFD handshake.
Initial output cannot dispatch a non-MEMFD action.
Initial output sequence is exactly one.
Reply kind, embedded state kind, and workspace kind must agree.
A terminal-looking reply with an active workspace must not transfer an fd or acknowledge an error.
Success and error terminals cannot be interchanged.
The new error continuation must retain the exact request error handle and corresponding actual exception.
The reply and workspace must both identify this frame.
Workspace input length must remain equal to the actual immutable bytes length.
Workspace progress must remain inside the actual input length.
A receipt checksum failure remains an unconfirmed native outcome.
A workspace checksum failure remains an unconfirmed native outcome.
The entire request including executable bytes must remain unchanged.
No acknowledgement after a changed policy output canary.
No acknowledgement after a changed policy workspace canary.
A status other than the complete policy receipt size cannot acknowledge delivery.
The selected error handle must identify the active actual exception, including close override.
Only the seven raw actions are admitted to raw dispatch.
MEMFD uses the unique no-descriptor sentinel.
MEMFD offset is zero.
MEMFD count and payload are empty.
MEMFD flags are the fixed ABI value.
Every other raw action has a nonnegative signed-int descriptor.
WRITE offset equals the validated workspace offset and lies within immutable input.
WRITE count equals remaining bytes and fits both the request allocation and input slice.
WRITE has no additional raw argument.
Actual immutable payload length equals the admitted WRITE count.
CHMOD mode is the fixed executable mode.
chmod requires the fixed zero offset before any raw buffer write.
chmod requires zero count and no raw payload before any raw buffer write.
add-seals requires the fixed zero offset before any raw buffer write.
add-seals requires zero count and no raw payload before any raw buffer write.
get-seals requires the fixed zero offset before any raw buffer write.
get-seals requires zero count and no raw payload before any raw buffer write.
close requires the fixed zero offset before any raw buffer write.
close requires zero count and no raw payload before any raw buffer write.
ADD_SEALS mask is the fixed complete mask.
GET_SEALS has the fixed zero raw argument.
PREAD capacity includes the one diagnostic extra byte and cannot be zero.
PREAD count cannot place a canary or kernel write beyond the real allocation.
PREAD count is bound to validated immutable input length plus one.
PREAD uses the fixed zero file offset.
PREAD has no additional raw argument.
CLOSE has no additional raw argument.
The complete request and canary must fit actual ctypes storage before writing.
The 96-byte result and canary must fit actual ctypes storage before writing.
The raw state header, PREAD capacity, and canary must fit actual ctypes storage before writing.
A confirmed PREAD copy must fit the policy readback region and leave its canary intact.

policy.source: real unchanged VM policy + declared fake kernel
policy.native: actual admitted HIA policy + actual native kernel; receipt mutation after actual policy return

prewrite.source: synthetic mechanical action projections with real fresh DeliveryRecord and bounded owned ctypes buffers; first-write trap, no native entry
prewrite.native: same mechanical guards on an actually admitted owner; no native entry for invalid inputs

actual_raw_loss.delivery: actual owned syscall completion before withheld or inconsistent receipt; process exit owns remaining descriptors

actual_negative.delivery: test closes its captured fd before actual GET_SEALS; actual kernel EBADF and ordinary HIA error/close continuation

actual_child_loss.delivery: native parent HIA with explicit fake parent kernel/audit/signal fixture; nested child executes actual native MEMFD before receipt loss
